content.text: The survivor is NH-533, the only duplicate with an active subscription. I'll apply the winning values to it first: the phone from NH-410 (verified 2026-09-01), the address from NH-472 (verified 2026-07-07), and opted_out marketing consent from NH-472.
All three field updates succeeded. Now I'll archive the two non-surviving duplicates into NH-533.

The three Noor Haddad records (born 1987-06-23) are merged into **NH-533**, which is the survivor.

- **Why NH-533 survives:** it is the only one of the three with an active subscription. The other two (NH-410 and NH-472) had none or a lapsed one, and archiving is not allowed for records with an active subscription.
- **Email:** kept as NH-533's own, `noor.h@fernhill.example`, since the survivor's email is always kept.
- **Phone:** set to `+44 7700 900410` from NH-410, verified 2026-09-01. This is more recent than NH-533's value, which was verified 2025-03-12.
- **Address:** set to `17 Bell Lane, Reading` from NH-472, verified 2026-07-07. NH-533 had no address, and NH-410's `4 Lime Walk, Oxford` was verified earlier (2024-03-03).
- **Marketing consent:** changed from opted_in to **opted_out**, because NH-472 is opted out and the policy says any opt-out wins.
- **Archived:** NH-410 and NH-472, both with `merged_into` set to NH-533.

Two things you may want to check. NH-533 was the only record with a legacy CRM source and a missing city, so its contact details came from the other records. The opt-out also changes NH-533's marketing status from what the customer had in that record.

CUS-9277 is merged into CUS-9210 and archived with CUS-9210 as its survivor.

Under merge policy MP-2026-7, CUS-9210 now has:
- **Email:** felix.moreau@example.com (unchanged). Its most recent change was a customer edit, which beats CUS-9277's staff edit.
- **Phone:** +33 6 55 01 02 77, taken from CUS-9277. Both last changes were by staff, and CUS-9277's (2026-05-05) is later than CUS-9210's (2026-01-15).
- **Address:** 3 Allee des Tilleuls, Lyon, taken from CUS-9277. Both last changes were by the customer, and CUS-9277's (2026-08-08) is later than CUS-9210's (2025-11-11).

The policy's source ranking would have kept CUS-9210's address, but the customer-change rule overrides it here.

The merge was done by updating the survivor's fields and then archiving the duplicate, since there is no single merge action. CUS-9210's existing notes ("Do not call before 10:00") were left as they were, and CUS-9277's notes ("No notes") were not carried over.

Both meetings are booked in Fern (North building, floor 2), which is the only room that fits all the constraints. Fern has a whiteboard, seats 4, and is free all day on 2026-11-03.

- **Design review** (BK-9901): 10:30–11:30 HQ time (New York). Attendees: Ana Ruiz, Ben Okafor, Chloe Marsh.
- **Decision sync** (BK-9902): 11:30–12:00 HQ time (New York). Attendees: Ana Ruiz, Ben Okafor, Tom Hale.

Everyone is free for their slot and inside their local working hours. Tom's London hours are 04:00–12:00 HQ time, so 11:30–12:00 falls at the end of his day (16:30–17:00 London).

The 10:30 start was the earliest option that worked. Chloe has a hiring sync until 10:30, so an earlier start wasn't possible. The other whiteboard rooms were unavailable: Birch, Dune, Lark and Cedar had conflicts, and Grove was booked for the leadership offsite.

10:00 is the earliest start when all three are free within their working hours. It only works because the cancelled demo freed Ana's and Ben's 10:00 slot. Haven is the video-conference room that seats three with the fewest seats; the other video rooms free at that time were Atlas (8 seats) and Grove (10 seats).

10:00 is the earliest slot where all three are free within working hours. Before the cancellation, Ana and Ben were tied up in the Vendor demo until 11:00, so the earliest common slot was later. Haven was the smallest video-conference room with three or more seats that was free at that time.

The Vendor demo was a weekly recurring booking, and I cancelled only BK-9701, the 2026-11-03 occurrence. I did not check whether later occurrences still exist, so they may need cancelling separately.

- **Cancelled:** BK-9701, the Vendor demo in Dune. It is a weekly series, so I only cancelled the 2026-11-03 occurrence. Any later occurrences are still booked and may need cancelling separately.
- **Why 10:00:** Before the cancellation, Ben was not free until 12:30 and no slot worked for all three. The cancellation freed Ana's and Ben's 10:00–11:00 slot, and 10:00 is the earliest time all three are free.
- **Room:** Haven is the smallest video-conference room that seats three and is free at that time. Birch, Ember, Atlas and Grove were either booked or larger.
- **Assumption:** I treated headquarters time as the same as the attendees' calendar time (America/New_York, UTC−5).

content.text:
All four open tickets that were in the intake queue are now routed. I routed them oldest first and checked each queue's load limit.

- **T-9104** (password reset link expired, opened 10-18 16:00) → **identity**. Its component is auth. Identity load goes from 3 to 4 of 6.
- **T-9101** (charge attempts time out, opened 10-19 08:00) → **payments**. Its component is payments_api. Payments load goes from 3 to 4 of 4, so it takes the last open place.
- **T-9102** (charged twice, opened 10-19 09:00) → **billing**. It is a billing_dispute, so it goes to billing whatever its component. Billing load goes from 0 to 1 of 10.
- **T-9103** (refund endpoint rejects valid IDs, opened 10-19 11:00) → **billing**. Its component is payments_api, but payments was already full at 4 of 4, so it went to payments' overflow queue, billing. Billing load goes from 1 to 2 of 10.

No other tickets were touched.
